falsifier: Any source edit that moves our pre-`stwu` `addi rD,rS,@SYM(ADDR16_LO)` to AFTER the `stmw` and into the callee-saved web directly, deleting the owed `mr` -- probe it with `python tools/gdl/probe.py game/audio/dcs dcsReadCalls --ops`, whose two clusters are the whole residual of that function, so any such edit shows immediately as count parity T242/O242. Equally falsifying: any MEMBER function whose target ALSO emits the LO before its `stwu` (which would make the target/ours split a scheduling coincidence rather than a class), or a re-run of the census below in which the r0-versus-named-volatile discriminator fails to separate the two groups.

value: MWCC GC 1.2.5, -O4,p. RECURRING PROLOGUE CLASS, censused. Both streams hoist the ADDR16_HA half of a file-scope symbol's address above the frame-opening `stwu` (`@0x4 lis r5,@SYM(ADDR16_HA)` is IDENTICAL in target and ours in every case measured). What differs is the ADDR16_LO half. When OURS emits the LO before the `stwu` into r0 specifically -- `@0xc addi r0,r5,@SYM(ADDR16_LO)` -- it cannot target a callee-saved register (none is saved yet), so it later pays a copy `@0x24 mr r31,r0`, and the target instead emits `@0x14 addi r31,r5,@SYM(ADDR16_LO)` AFTER the `stmw`, straight into the web. The residual is therefore always exactly one surplus `mr`, count-asymmetric by one, with the paired `fndiff --ops` signature `insert T[3:3]@c-c=[] O[3:4]@c-10=['addi']` plus `replace T[..]=['addi'] O[..]=['mr'] [SHIFTABLE]`. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE DESTINATION REGISTER, NOT THE HOISTING. Census over 36 functions in 15 TUs at commit 71de6e8e7 (NC_scratch/nc_prologue_census.py, zero builds -- it reads the aligned `fnasm 0x0:0x40 --diff` view): ELEVEN functions emit an ADDR16_LO before the `stwu`, and they split cleanly in two. FOUR write it into r0 and every one of those owes the `mr` -- game/audio/dcs::dcsReadCalls (`@0xc addi r0,r5,@lbl_80116F58(ADDR16_LO)`, target `@0x1c addi r31,r5,LO`, T242/O243), game/mb/mb_model::MBOX_LoadModelFixed (`@0xc addi r0,r5,@lbl_80115DA8(ADDR16_LO)`, target `@0x18 addi r31,r5,LO`, T124/O125), game/ui/auxscreen::init_mapscreen (`@0xc addi r0,r5,@lbl_8023DFD0(ADDR16_LO)`, target `@0x14 addi r31,r5,LO`, T185/O184) and game/sound/sounds::MapMusicStart (`@0xc addi r0,r3,@sSpeechNameBuf(ADDR16_LO)`). SEVEN write it into a NAMED volatile and none of them owes a copy, because those values are consumed as call arguments or temps rather than parked in a web -- game/ui/auxscreen::do_mapscreen (`addi r4,r4,LO`), game/game/player::setup_player_display (`addi r5,r4,@gPlayers(ADDR16_LO)`), game/boss/bosscam::TriggerCamUpdate (`addi r3,r3,LO`), game/shop/shop::shop_setup (`addi r0,r3,LO` but no owed copy), game/audio/adstream::AdsPutBuffer (`addi r6,r6,LO`), game/world/world::StartWorldLoad (`addi r5,r4,LO`) and game/sound/sounds::AudioBuildMusicName (`addi r4,r4,@sSpeechNameBuf(ADDR16_LO)`). The remaining 25 screened functions emit no pre-frame LO at all. THE SYMBOL IS NOT THE CARRIER: `sSpeechNameBuf` appears on BOTH sides of the split (MapMusicStart is a member, AudioBuildMusicName is not), so the class is a property of what the address is ASSIGNED TO, not of the object addressed. WHAT DOES NOT REACH IT, measured. (a) DECLARATION ORDER IS CATEGORICALLY DEAD ON A MEMBER: on dcsReadCalls, moving `char* strs = lbl_80116F58;` from first to third in the initialised-local list produced `NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL-PROOF unit=game/audio/dcs fn=dcsReadCalls bytes=dacc8b57ae1e real=125 insns=T242/O243 multiset=1t head=71de6e8e7` -- the object bytes did not move at all, so the edit never reached codegen and no respelling of the same construct can, and the two initialised pointer locals are proved to sit in the same allocator class. (b) `#pragma opt_propagation off` IS NOT THE CAUSE: removing the bracket that surrounds init_mapscreen left the .text completely unchanged (real 99, T185/O184, multiset 5t, every cluster including both prologue clusters identical), while moving the object's extab/extabindex -- so the pragma is load-bearing for that TU's exception tables and irrelevant to this class. (c) DECLARATION-WITH-INITIALISER VERSUS BODY-ASSIGNMENT is also a proved boundary, on game/game/player::draw_power_meter: declaring `Player* p; s32* table;` and assigning both at the top of the body was NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL to the initialiser form. WHAT DOES REACH IT, once, and only partly: on draw_power_meter, EXCHANGING the order of two initialised locals of DIFFERENT construct classes (a macro-computed record pointer against a plain symbol address) removed one of two hoisted `lis` and took real 60 -> 58 -- so the class boundary the NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL probes prove is between locals of the SAME class, and a cross-class exchange is the one source lever measured to move a prologue at all. CONSEQUENCE: on a member, do not spend probes on declaration order, declaration form, or `opt_propagation`. The residual is one instruction of count asymmetry, so claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-a-count-asymmetric-residual.20260831.v1 bars the postprocessor path too; treat a member as a named one-instruction residual unless a cross-class declaration exchange is available, and re-run the census command above before believing this population, which is a floor over 36 screened functions and not an image-wide total.
